title: DigitalOcean Insights is now generally available: Unified observability across every layer of your stack
summary: DigitalOcean Insights is now generally available, giving you a unified observability stack build into supported DigitalOcean products. Platform metrics, logs, and traces are sent from managed products with no instrumentation required.
body_markdown:
Observability is critical for running software in production. It helps teams understand whether a service is healthy, why a request slowed down, and what changed before an incident began. Answering those questions draws on more than one signal. Metrics show that behavior has changed, logs record what happened, and traces show where along a request’s path it happened. These signals are most useful when you can move from one to the next without losing context. As a stack grows to span clusters, databases, and agents, a unified view across every layer allows a team to keep pace with the system it operates.


DigitalOcean Insights gives you a unified observability stack built into the DigitalOcean products you already use, so you don’t have to take it on as a separate project. In October, we announced[the public preview of Insights](https://www.digitalocean.com/blog/introducing-insights) , which brought metrics, logs, and traces from Kubernetes, App Platform, Managed Agents, and our inference products into one place, with no instrumentation required.


Today, we are announcing the general availability (GA) of DigitalOcean Insights. Insights now covers every layer of your stack, is built on[OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) (OTel), and gives you the controls to run it in production. This post walks through what’s new at GA and what changes if you used Insights during public preview or use DigitalOcean Monitoring today.


## Built into every layer of your stack


In public preview, Insights supported a core set of DigitalOcean products, focused on where your agents and applications run. Starting today, Insights supports DigitalOcean products across every layer of your stack, including the data services and networking those workloads depend on. This includes compute (Droplets, Kubernetes, App Platform, Functions, and MicroVMs), databases and data services (PostgreSQL and MySQL on the Advanced tier, MongoDB, Valkey, Kafka, and OpenSearch), networking (Load Balancers and NAT Gateway), and AI (inference, Managed Agents, and Knowledge Bases). See[Insights documentation](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/insights/) for the full list of supported products and the signals each one sends.


Every supported product sends platform metrics to Insights at no charge, so you start with a baseline view of your stack. Logs and traces add the detail you need to investigate an issue, and you can turn them on for each resource when you create it or later in Insights settings.


For example, if an App Platform service is responding slowly, its request duration chart in Insights shows when the slowdown began. With logs turned on, one click takes you to that service’s logs for the same time window, so you can see what went wrong without leaving the page. Metrics for the managed database behind the service can sit on the same dashboard, so you can also tell whether the database is the cause. The same applies to the MicroVMs your agents run code in. Each MicroVM sends metrics, logs, and traces, so you can follow what an agent did inside its environment with the same tools you use for the rest of your stack.


## Built on OpenTelemetry


Insights uses OTel as the common format for collecting all telemetry. Metrics, logs, and traces from every supported product arrive in a single data model, rather than in a different shape for each product. As a result, a metric, a log, and a trace from the same resource line up in Insights without you having to match them by hand.


OTel also keeps your data open and portable. Your telemetry is stored in an open format rather than a proprietary one. With the new telemetry export feature, you can also send logs ingested in Insights in near real time to a third-party tool or an endpoint you run yourself, and see the connection and error status of each export.


## Built to run in production


Observability must go beyond investigating issues. It also needs to alert your on-call team, help you keep spend within plan, and keep an audit trail of changes. Insights provides the following controls to help with each of these goals.


**Alerts that reach your team.** You can now send alerts to a webhook in addition to email, so they reach the incident management and chat tools your team already uses. Alert history keeps a record of past alerts in the control panel.


**Spend you can see and control.** The Usage view shows ingestion for each resource, with a CSV download and a shortcut to create a spend alert. Settings lists every resource with a billable signal turned on, with a toggle for each. You can also adjust the trace sampling rate for your team without redeploying anything.


**Telemetry retention controls.** You can extend the retention duration for metrics, logs, and traces beyond the defaults, with a separate setting for each signal that applies across your team.


**Audit trail of changes.** Your team’s security history records changes to alert rules, telemetry exports, sampling, and retention, alongside the rest of your account activity.


## Built for code and agents


Teams that manage their infrastructure as code expect the same from their observability setup. Alert rules created in a console are hard to review and tend to drift between environments. The REST API, SDKs, and doctl cover metrics, logs, traces, and alerts, so you can define alert rules alongside the rest of your infrastructure, review changes the way you review code, and keep alerting consistent across environments.


Teams increasingly use agents for this work as well. Coding agents already write and ship code, and debugging that code requires the same telemetry your team relies on. The Insights MCP server gives agents direct access to that telemetry. For example, an agent investigating a failed deploy or a slow endpoint can query metrics, search logs, and retrieve traces directly, without you copying them into a chat. Agents can also list alerts and create or edit alert rules after you confirm the change, so you stay in control of your account.


## Pricing


Platform metrics are available at no charge for every supported product. You pay for the logs and traces you choose to collect, and each team gets 5 GB of logs and traces every month at no charge. Billing for Insights begins today, November 19, 2026. See[Insights pricing](https://www.digitalocean.com/pricing/insights) for more details.


What Price


Platform metrics No charge


Logs and traces ingestion $0.50/GB, with the first 5 GB each month at no charge per team (shared by logs and traces)


Extended retention (optional) $0.025/GB per month, on uncompressed data


Telemetry export (logs, optional) $0.10/GB


Custom telemetry (private preview) $0.10/GB


## Custom telemetry (private preview)


Platform telemetry explains how your infrastructure behaves. Your applications know the rest, such as checkout conversions, queue depth, or the errors your code logs. With custom telemetry, you can bring that data into Insights and view it alongside telemetry from the DigitalOcean products your applications run on.


Because Insights is built on OTel, you can send custom telemetry without a proprietary agent. You can instrument your applications with an OTel SDK, or point an OTel Collector you already run at a regional Insights endpoint over OTLP/HTTP, using an API token scoped for ingestion. Custom metrics work in Metrics Explorer, dashboards, alerts, and PromQL queries. Custom logs from your applications, hosts, containers, or Kubernetes workloads appear in Logs Explorer next to platform logs.


Custom metrics and custom logs are available in private preview today, and we’re enabling access for a small group of teams. If you want to use custom telemetry, request access using the[private preview access form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScYqTG9JDoSg1M7QBYzOMtV74xX5HCGzM9n_0NeHMWpHhGuBA/viewform?usp=dialog) .


## Get started


Insights brings every layer of your stack into one view. It’s built on OTel and gives you the controls to run it in production. To get started,[open Insights in the control panel](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/insights) ,[read the documentation](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/insights/) , or see[Insights pricing](https://www.digitalocean.com/pricing/insights) .


**Important note for DigitalOcean Monitoring users:** DigitalOcean Monitoring is now part of Insights. Your existing Droplet metrics, resource alerts, and metrics agent continue to work under Insights, without any action from you. Some alert evaluation windows change, so review your existing alerts in Insights.


**Important note for public preview participants:** If your resources sent logs or traces during public preview, Insights will keep collecting them at GA and bill for them starting November 19 unless you turn them off. To stop collecting a signal, turn it off for that resource in Insights settings. Data you’ve already collected stays until its retention period ends.
